classification.difficultyReason: Reconciling both claims requires distinguishing age recorded in completed years from continuously varying elapsed time. This reframes the taught discrete/continuous distinction through recording precision rather than applying it to an unambiguous example.

content.prompt: Zach says, “Age is an example of discrete data.” Ed says, “Age is continuous data.” Suggest why each person thinks what they do.

answer.short: Zach: completed whole years give discrete records. Ed: exact elapsed time since birth is continuous.
answer.worked: Zach means age recorded in completed whole years. Ed means the underlying elapsed time since birth, which varies continuously.
